+//! The plasma profile operation's stored parameters (#670): what the
+//! op keeps, as heights and plain numbers - resolved into the motion
+//! crate's `plasma::PlasmaParams` at generation.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own parameter set over public plasma practice -
+//! Hypertherm's cut-direction guidance, the LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §13
+//! small-hole rule, and Tormach's public 1300PL manual / PathPilot post
+//! guidelines (feed, pierce height, cut height and delay are optional:
+//! blank leaves them to the controller's AutoFS).
+
+use super::height::Height;
+
+/// Where the kerf offset is made: walked by the computer (the default -
+/// the path is the torch centre), or posted as G41/G42 for the control
+/// to offset (the CL then carries the part contour beside the centre
+/// path, with straight engage / cancel leads longer than the kerf
+/// radius - Tormach's PathPilot rule).
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum PlasmaComp {
+    #[default]
+    Computer,
+    Control,
+}
+
+/// The plasma profile's parameters. Every `Option` blank is the
+/// controller's decision, never a guessed number.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct PlasmaOp {
+    /// The torch-off travel plane.
+    pub clearance_z: Height,
+    /// The plate's top: the plane the cut rides (plus the cut height,
+    /// when stated).
+    pub top_z: Height,
+    /// The plate's bottom: with the top it states the thickness the
+    /// small-hole rule reads. Nothing steps down to it - a plasma cut
+    /// goes through in one pass.
+    pub bottom_z: Height,
+    /// The kerf width override, mm; `None` reads the torch tool's
+    /// diameter (its kerf width).
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    pub comp: PlasmaComp,
+    /// Outer contours counter-clockwise and holes clockwise - the
+    /// override of the square-edge-on-the-part default, stated in the
+    /// path's notes and its CL header.
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    /// Lead-in / lead-out length, mm (an arc in computer compensation,
+    /// a straight line under G41/G42); 0 = none.
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    /// Holes under this diameter (or under 1.5x the plate thickness)
+    /// take the small-hole rule, mm.
+    pub small_hole_dia: f64,
+    /// The small-hole feed factor, (0, 1] - 0.65 by default.
+    pub small_hole_feed: f64,
+    /// A small hole's overburn past its start, mm; 0 = none.
+    pub overburn: f64,
+    /// Cut feed, mm/min; `None` = the controller's material table.
+    pub feed: Option<f64>,
+    /// Pierce height / cut height above the plate, mm, and the pierce
+    /// delay, s; `None` = the controller decides.
+    pub pierce_height: Option<f64>,
+    pub cut_height: Option<f64>,
+    pub pierce_delay: Option<f64>,
+}
+
+impl PlasmaOp {
+    /// Structural sanity (no world): every number finite and in range.
+    /// The motion crate's door repeats the refusals by name at
+    /// generation; this is the command door's yes / no.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn is_sane(&self) -> bool {
+        let nneg = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0;
+        let opt = |v: Option<f64>| v.is_none_or(nneg);
+        self.clearance_z.is_sane()
+            && self.top_z.is_sane()
+            && self.bottom_z.is_sane()
+            && self.kerf.is_none_or(|k| k.is_finite() && k > 0.0)
+            && nneg(self.lead_in)
+            && nneg(self.lead_out)
+            && nneg(self.small_hole_dia)
+            && self.small_hole_feed.is_finite()
+            && self.small_hole_feed > 0.0
+            && self.small_hole_feed <= 1.0
+            && nneg(self.overburn)
+            && self.feed.is_none_or(|f| f.is_finite() && f > 0.0)
+            && opt(self.pierce_height)
+            && opt(self.cut_height)
+            && opt(self.pierce_delay)
+    }
+}

+//! The plasma profile's file mirror (#670): the op's parameters as
+//! plain keys (blank options absent), and the cached path's plasma
+//! record (kerf, torch spans, nesting) beside the moves - the additive
+//! law of the comps / threads / probes keys: absent is none.
+//! Provenance: our own file format (`project/mod.rs`); the names are ours.
+
+use super::*;
+
+use crate::cl::{ContourRole, Move, PlasmaCut, TorchSpan};
+use crate::operation::{PlasmaComp, PlasmaOp};
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum PlasmaCompDto {
+    Computer,
+    Control,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct PlasmaDto {
+    pub clearance_z: HeightDto,
+    pub top_z: HeightDto,
+    pub bottom_z: HeightDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    pub comp: PlasmaCompDto,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    pub small_hole_dia: f64,
+    pub small_hole_feed: f64,
+    pub overburn: f64,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub feed: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub pierce_height: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub cut_height: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub pierce_delay: Option<f64>,
+}
+
+impl PlasmaDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_op(p: &PlasmaOp) -> Self {
+        PlasmaDto {
+            clearance_z: p.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: p.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: p.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: p.kerf,
+            comp: match p.comp {
+                PlasmaComp::Computer => PlasmaCompDto::Computer,
+                PlasmaComp::Control => PlasmaCompDto::Control,
+            },
+            reversed: p.reversed,
+            lead_in: p.lead_in,
+            lead_out: p.lead_out,
+            small_hole_dia: p.small_hole_dia,
+            small_hole_feed: p.small_hole_feed,
+            overburn: p.overburn,
+            feed: p.feed,
+            pierce_height: p.pierce_height,
+            cut_height: p.cut_height,
+            pierce_delay: p.pierce_delay,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn to_params(&self) -> OpParams {
+        OpParams::PlasmaProfile(PlasmaOp {
+            clearance_z: self.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: self.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: self.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: self.kerf,
+            comp: match self.comp {
+                PlasmaCompDto::Computer => PlasmaComp::Computer,
+                PlasmaCompDto::Control => PlasmaComp::Control,
+            },
+            reversed: self.reversed,
+            lead_in: self.lead_in,
+            lead_out: self.lead_out,
+            small_hole_dia: self.small_hole_dia,
+            small_hole_feed: self.small_hole_feed,
+            overburn: self.overburn,
+            feed: self.feed,
+            pierce_height: self.pierce_height,
+            cut_height: self.cut_height,
+            pierce_delay: self.pierce_delay,
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// One cached torch span.
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct TorchSpanDto {
+    pub contour: u32,
+    /// `outer` / `inner` / `open`.
+    pub role: String,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub parent: Option<u32>,
+    pub on: u64,
+    pub off: u64,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub small: Option<f64>,
+}
+
+/// The cached plasma record of a path.
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct PlasmaCutDto {
+    pub kerf: f64,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub pierce_height: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub cut_height: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub pierce_delay: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub auto_feed: bool,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub torches: Vec<TorchSpanDto>,
+}
+
+impl PlasmaCutDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_cut(p: &PlasmaCut) -> Self {
+        PlasmaCutDto {
+            kerf: p.kerf,
+            control_comp: p.control_comp,
+            pierce_height: p.pierce_height,
+            cut_height: p.cut_height,
+            pierce_delay: p.pierce_delay,
+            auto_feed: p.auto_feed,
+            reversed: p.reversed,
+            torches: p
+                .torches
+                .iter()
+                .map(|t| TorchSpanDto {
+                    contour: t.contour,
+                    role: t.role.word().to_ascii_lowercase(),
+                    parent: t.parent,
+                    on: t.on as u64,
+                    off: t.off as u64,
+                    small: t.small,
+                })
+                .collect(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The record of a loaded path - or none when any span does not sit
+    /// on the moves (the op then reads stale and re-generates; a torch
+    /// record is never half-trusted).
+    pub(super) fn load(&self, moves: &[Move]) -> Option<PlasmaCut> {
+        let torches = self
+            .torches
+            .iter()
+            .map(|t| {
+                Some(TorchSpan {
+                    contour: t.contour,
+                    role: ContourRole::from_word(&t.role.to_ascii_uppercase())?,
+                    parent: t.parent,
+                    on: usize::try_from(t.on).ok()?,
+                    off: usize::try_from(t.off).ok()?,
+                    small: t.small,
+                })
+            })
+            .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let cut = PlasmaCut {
+            kerf: self.kerf,
+            control_comp: self.control_comp,
+            pierce_height: self.pierce_height,
+            cut_height: self.cut_height,
+            pierce_delay: self.pierce_delay,
+            auto_feed: self.auto_feed,
+            reversed: self.reversed,
+            torches,
+        };
+        cut.is_sane(moves).then_some(cut)
+    }
+}

+//! The machine KIND: what a `.mch` declares itself to be (mill, lathe,
+//! mill-turn, plasma), and the axis-inventory inference for files that
+//! declare nothing.
+//!
+//! Provenance: general machine-tool practice (a mill moves a cutter in
+//! X/Y/Z, a lathe turns the part under an X/Z tool, a mill-turn does
+//! both); the plasma kind (#669) from Tormach's public 1300PL
+//! Operator's Manual UM10720 v1223A §2 (an X/Y gantry whose Z is the
+//! torch lifter) - behaviour only, our own words. Split out of `def`
+//! (#669) along the kind seam, so `def` stays the plain data.
+
+use super::def::{AxisLimits, Machine};
+
+/// What a machine is, inferred from its axis inventory (M3.2 stage E -
+/// the workspaces-by-kind law, refined by M5.1 stage A). Provenance:
+/// general machine-tool practice - a mill moves a cutter in X, Y and
+/// Z; a lathe turns the part and moves a tool in X and Z only; a
+/// mill-turn does both, which an ordinary file reveals as a Y axis
+/// with a TURNING rotary among its axes: one whose direction is the Z
+/// column (a C table) or unstated. A rotary that states a LEANING
+/// direction (an A or B head or trunnion) tilts a milling cutter and
+/// turns nothing - a Y machine with only those is still a [`Kind::Mill`],
+/// five axes of it. The inference stays deliberately the minimal
+/// honest one: anything the axis list cannot decide - an unnamed file,
+/// a file with no X/Z pair - reads [`Kind::Mill`], because a mill is
+/// what every assumption in this codebase currently is, and an
+/// invented lathe workspace would be the silent wrong answer.
+///
+/// [`Kind::Plasma`] (#669) is DECLARED only, never inferred: a plasma
+/// table's X/Y/Z inventory is a mill's, so a file that does not say
+/// "plasma" reads as the mill its axes describe. The declaration
+/// carries the plasma rules (no spindle, no rotary, Z is the torch
+/// lifter - `plasma::refusals`), so the word is never decoration.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum Kind {
+    Mill,
+    Lathe,
+    MillTurn,
+    /// A plasma cutting table (#669): X and Y cut, Z lifts the torch
+    /// (the control owns it - pierce height, cut height, THC), and no
+    /// spindle turns.
+    Plasma,
+}
+
+impl Kind {
+    /// The word the pages and tips use for the kind.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Kind::Mill => "milling",
+            Kind::Lathe => "turning",
+            Kind::MillTurn => "mill-turning",
+            Kind::Plasma => "plasma cutting",
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The word a machine file writes for this kind - the canonical
+    /// spelling the editor's combo emits, the subset `from_word`
+    /// accepts.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Kind::Mill => "mill",
+            Kind::Lathe => "lathe",
+            Kind::MillTurn => "mill-turn",
+            Kind::Plasma => "plasma",
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Read a declared kind word (M3.3 stage C): case- and
+    /// punctuation-tolerant over the public vocabulary (a mill is
+    /// also "milling", a lathe also "turning", and the hybrid's
+    /// hyphen is optional). `None` = not a kind word; the caller
+    /// refuses rather than guessing, because a typo'd declaration
+    /// that silently inferred would be the declaration law undone.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_word(w: &str) -> Option<Kind> {
+        let n: String = w
+            .chars()
+            .filter(|c| c.is_alphanumeric())
+            .flat_map(char::to_lowercase)
+            .collect();
+        match n.as_str() {
+            "mill" | "milling" => Some(Kind::Mill),
+            "lathe" | "turning" | "turn" => Some(Kind::Lathe),
+            "millturn" | "turnmill" | "millturning" | "turningmill" => Some(Kind::MillTurn),
+            "plasma" | "plasmacutting" | "plasmatable" => Some(Kind::Plasma),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The geometric tilt question (M5.1 stage A): can this machine lean
+/// its tool? `machine.rtcp`'s law, restated for the checker's parsed
+/// axes - true iff some rotary states a direction that is not the Z
+/// column (z² < 0.99·(x²+y²+z²)). A C table is not tilt; a trunnion
+/// or a tilting head is. An UNSTATED direction tilts nothing this
+/// app may verify against: capability must be claimed, never
+/// assumed.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn can_tilt(machine: &Machine) -> bool {
+    machine.axes.iter().any(|a| a.rotary && is_tilt_axis(a))
+}
+
+/// Is `a` a rotary whose stated direction LEANS (off the Z column)?
+fn is_tilt_axis(a: &AxisLimits) -> bool {
+    a.axis
+        .is_some_and(|d| d[2] * d[2] < 0.99 * (d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1] + d[2] * d[2]))
+}
+
+/// The machine's kind (M3.3 stage C): what the file DECLARES wins;
+/// a silent file falls to the axis-inventory law of M3.2 stage E
+/// (below), which the same files always produced. An unparseable
+/// declaration cannot arrive here - `parse_mch` refuses it at the
+/// front door and `is_sane` gates hand-edited project files - so by
+/// the time a Machine exists, a stated kind is a known word.
+///
+/// Rotary axes alone do not make a mill-turn: a turning center with
+/// a C axis still has no Y, and the file says "lathe". And (M5.1 A)
+/// a TILTING rotary makes no more a mill-turn than a table does:
+/// A and B heads and trunnions lean a milling cutter without ever
+/// spinning a part for turning. The turning question is the same
+/// geometry `can_tilt` answers, inverted - a rotary counts toward
+/// "turning" unless its stated direction says lean; unstated
+/// rotaries stay counted, the stage-E law for the files that
+/// predate the vectors.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn kind(machine: Option<&Machine>) -> Kind {
+    let Some(m) = machine else {
+        return Kind::Mill; // the unstated machine is today's document
+    };
+    if let Some(w) = &m.kind
+        && let Some(k) = Kind::from_word(w)
+    {
+        return k;
+    }
+    let has = |n: &str| m.axes.iter().any(|a| a.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n));
+    let stated = |a: &AxisLimits| {
+        a.rotary || ["A", "B", "C"].iter().any(|r| a.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(r))
+    };
+    let turning = m.axes.iter().any(|a| stated(a) && !is_tilt_axis(a));
+    match (has("Y"), has("X"), has("Z"), turning) {
+        (true, _, _, true) => Kind::MillTurn,
+        (true, _, _, false) => Kind::Mill,
+        (false, true, true, _) => Kind::Lathe,
+        _ => Kind::Mill,
+    }
+}
+

+
+## Plasma records (`.cl` v5, #670)
+
+A plasma profile's path (`OpType::PlasmaProfile`, the torch on a
+plasma table) carries `Toolpath::plasma` ([`cl::PlasmaCut`]): the kerf
+the moves were offset by, the torch on / off per contour, each
+contour's role and the contour it lies in. The `.cl` dump writes it as
+comment-prefixed records (`cl::text::to_text` / `from_text`, and the
+golden writer `common::gen_to_cltext`, byte for byte), so the header
+reads `; HSMW-CL v5` and a reader that knows only the legacy grammar -
+the post's stream parser included - skips them. The moves stay the
+torch-centre truth (every lit move stands kerf / 2 off the part on the
+waste side, or on the centre line of an open run); the records say
+what the moves alone cannot. Pinned by
+`crates/app/tests/golden/plasma_plate_with_holes.cl`.
+
+| line | meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `; PLASMA KERF<µm> [CONTROL] [PIERCE<µm>] [CUTH<µm>] [DELAY<ms>] [AUTOFEED] [REVERSED]` | the header, once, right after `START`. `KERF` the kerf width (the torch tool's diameter or the op's override) - required. `CONTROL`: the control compensates (the G41/G42 spans ride the path's comps - see `COMP` above - with straight engage / cancel leads at least the kerf radius long, Tormach's PathPilot rule); absent: the offset is in the moves. `PIERCE` / `CUTH` the pierce and cut heights above the plate, `DELAY` the pierce delay - each present only when the op states it (absent = the controller's AutoFS decides). `AUTOFEED`: the op states no feed - the lit moves carry no `F`, the controller's material table feeds. `REVERSED`: the cut direction was overridden (outer contours counter-clockwise, holes clockwise; the default is outer CW / holes CCW, Hypertherm's square edge on the part) |
+| `; TORCH ON C<id> OUTER\|INNER\|OPEN [PARENT<id>] [SMALL<f×1000>]` | the torch is struck before the next motion record (the pierce: the tool already stands at the cut plane over the pierce point; the controller's G15/G16 own the Z). `C<id>` the contour's id - ids run in CUT ORDER from 0. `OUTER` a part's outer edge (waste outside), `INNER` a hole (waste inside), `OPEN` an open run cut on its centre line. `PARENT<id>` the closed contour it lies inside (a hole names its part's outline; an island part inside a hole names the hole; absent = none). `SMALL<f>` the small-hole rule cut it (LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §13): a straight lead-in from near the centre, no lead-out, an optional overburn, the cut feed times `f/1000` (650 = 65 %) |
+| `; TORCH OFF C<id>` | the torch goes out after the previous motion record (the lead-out's end, or a small hole's overburn end); names the same id as its `ON` |
+
+Laws (the reader refuses by line, `PlasmaCut::is_sane`): one header
+before any `TORCH`; spans never nest or overlap and appear in cut
+order; every lit record is a feed or arc, never a rapid; ids are
+unique and every `PARENT` names a contour of the path; a torch never
+put out is an error. Cut order is the generator's law and the
+records make it checkable: every contour's `OFF` comes before its
+parent's `ON` - an island before its hole, a hole before the outline
+that frees the part.
+
+For the post (#671) and the plasma verification laws (#672): the
+`.cnc` stream does not carry these records yet - posting a plasma
+table is refused until the plasma post ships (`posting::PLASMA_POSTS`
+is empty), and the post owns voicing them (`M200`/`M207..M211`,
+`G15`/`G16`, `M205`, `G30`; [UM] §7).

+## #669 - a plasma machine kind and the Tormach 1300PL
+
+Sources (clean room, behaviour only): Tormach *1300PL Operator's Manual*
+UM10720 v1223A ([UM]), the 1300PL spec sheet 03/24 ([SS]), Tormach's

+## #670 - a plasma profile operation
+
+Sources (clean room, behaviour only): Hypertherm's published cut-quality
+guidance (cut direction), the LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §13 (small holes),
+Tormach's *1300PL Operator's Manual* UM10720 v1223A and *PathPilot Post
+Processor Guidelines* (AutoFS, G41/G42 entry, kerf ≈ 1.5x orifice) - as
+cited in the #621 research comment. No commercial CAM output was read.
+
+**1. The torch is a tool kind; its diameter is the kerf.** `ToolKind::Torch`
+(#669 decision 3): `diameter` = kerf width (the editor labels it "Kerf
+width"), `corner_r` must be 0, `rpm` must be 0 - `Tool::is_sane` relaxes
+rpm > 0 for the torch only, and a torch stating an rpm is refused by name
+(`Tool::torch_refusal`) at `AddTool`, `ChangeTool` and the tool-library
+reader. The op may override the kerf (`PlasmaOp::kerf`, blank = the
+torch's) - one torch runs many materials. A starter `PT-KERF-150` (1.5 mm)
+ships in the catalog. *Dropped:* a separate kerf field on the tool (the
+diameter already feeds every offset and the G41 D register).
+
+**2. A new family and section, appended.** `Family::Plasma` /
+`Section::Plasma` / `OpType::PlasmaProfile` (stored id 39, appended - no
+kind id moves). `Family::admits` pairs Plasma with `Kind::Plasma` only; the
+mill-turn admits Mill and Turn, no longer `_` (a mill-turn strikes no arc).
+The family door's wording names both ways ("plasma cutting work ... mount
+a plasma table"; "a plasma table cuts only plasma operations (a Plasma
+Profile)"). The machine check's `cuts_plasma` answers true for the family.
+
+**3. The op is its own generator, like the probe.** `run_job_arms` returns
+early into `operation::plasma_op` -> `motion::plasma`. The milling verify
+laws (tangency, reach, depth, the stock sim) have no torch to judge, so the
+row's mode is `Engrave` and the stock sim / rest skip torch paths (named in
+the comments); the generator certifies its own **kerf law**: every lit move
+of a closed contour, chord-sampled every 0.25 mm, keeps the kerf disc off
+the part's through-silhouette (part offset by kerf/2 − 0.025 mm) or the op
+is refused by name. The plasma verdicts proper (cut order, kerf crossings,
+tip-ups) are #672's, from the CL records below. *Why not the mill verify
+with a fake cutter:* its laws assume a spindle column and a stock model a
+through-cut does not have; a pass from them would be a green that never
+looked.
+
+**4. Geometry: the picks the contour's way, else the through-silhouette.**
+A selection source resolves through `selection_geometry_impl` like the 2D
+Contour (closed rings AND open runs). An entity / stock source cuts every
+ring of the model's XY silhouette (`slice::project`) - a through-cut can
+only make through features, so a blind pocket is correctly absent. Each
+closed ring's role is read from the part: material just inside it -> an
+outer edge, air -> a hole (so a hole rim picked alone is still a hole);
+with no part (empty silhouette) nesting parity decides, said in the notes.
+Parents are the smallest enclosing closed ring. Open runs are cut on their
+centre line (no side, no leads), noted and exempt from the kerf law.
+
+**5. Kerf in the computer by default; G41/G42 as the option.** Computer:
+the moves ARE the offset ring (outline grown by kerf/2, hole shrunk by
+kerf/2, clipper2 round joins). Control: the moves stay the same centre
+truth and a `CompSpan` per contour carries the PART contour with straight
+engage / cancel leads; the door refuses a lead shorter than the kerf
+radius by name (PathPilot: the entry must be longer than the tool radius -
+ours is lead + kerf/2 ≥ 2 x radius). Small holes under control comp ride
+the computer's offset (noted): the hole rule has no lead-out to carry G40.
+*Dropped:* arc leads under G41/G42 (most controls refuse comp start / stop
+on an arc).
+
+**6. Direction: outer CW, holes CCW; `reversed` flips both and is stated**
+in the path notes and the CL header (`REVERSED`). Open runs keep their
+picked direction.
+
+**7. Leads.** Arc lead-in / lead-out on the waste side, tangent to the
+contour at the midpoint of the offset ring's longest edge (never a corner);
+the parameter is the arc LENGTH of a quarter arc (radius 2L/π). A lead with
+no room (it would bring the kerf onto the part - a narrow hole, an island)
+is halved up to four times, the shortening noted; past that the contour is
+refused by name. Default 5 mm in, 3 mm out.
+
+**8. Small holes (Primer §13).** A hole is small when its area-equivalent
+diameter is under `small_hole_dia` (default 32 mm) or under 1.5x the plate
+thickness (top − bottom). It pierces at the hole's centroid, leads in
+straight to the nearest point of the kerf ring (perpendicular to it, ≤ the
+radius), takes no lead-out, runs on `overburn` mm (default 0 - optional)
+and feeds at `small_hole_feed` (default 65 %, the band's middle). A
+centroid outside its own cut (a C-shaped hole) is refused by name.
+
+**9. Cut order: post-order of the nesting tree** - every contour after
+everything inside it (island, then its hole, then the outline); siblings by
+lowest-then-leftmost point, deterministic. Contour ids in the CL are the
+cut order.
+
+**10. Z and the controller's numbers.** The lit moves ride the plate top
+(+ the cut height when stated); rapids at the clearance plane; the descent
+to the cut plane is a rapid before `TORCH ON` (the controller's G15/G16 own
+it). Feed, pierce height, cut height and delay are `Option`s - blank is the
+controller's AutoFS; a blank feed leaves the lit moves without `F` and the
+header says `AUTOFEED`.
+
+**11. The CL records for #671 / #672** (docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md, "Plasma
+records"): `Toolpath::plasma: Option<PlasmaCut>` -
+`; PLASMA KERF<µm> [CONTROL] [PIERCE<µm>] [CUTH<µm>] [DELAY<ms>] [AUTOFEED] [REVERSED]`,
+`; TORCH ON C<id> OUTER|INNER|OPEN [PARENT<id>] [SMALL<f×1000>]` before the
+first lit move, `; TORCH OFF C<id>` after the last. Comment-prefixed, so
+the legacy reader and the post's stream parser skip them; `.cl` v5. They
+round-trip the text dump and the project's path cache (`plasma` key,
+additive). *For #671:* the `.cnc` dump does not yet emit them - the post
+owns that, and posting a plasma table stays refused until it ships. A
+cached path whose plasma record fails its sanity check on load keeps none;
+the plasma post must refuse a Plasma Profile path that carries no record.
+
+**12. Owed / not judged here:** material left by a slot or inlet narrower
+than the kerf on an OUTER contour that the offset bridges without
+enclosing (an enclosed gap or a pinched hole IS refused) - #672's
+material-left law; kerf crossings between contours and tip-up risk - #672;
+pierce-point placement relative to previous cuts - #672.
